bib.title: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Tables 29 and 37 (per-task BIG-bench and rest-of-MMLU cells) and long generated-text examples in A.8 skimmed

question: Can a language model trained on a small, curated scientific corpus store, combine and reason about scientific knowledge better than general models?
hypothesis: A high-quality curated corpus (with prompts and special tokens for modalities) lets a smaller model beat much larger general models on scientific tasks and tolerate repeated epochs.
contributions: Galactica models from 125M to 120B trained on a curated 106B-token scientific corpus
Prompt pre-training mixed with the corpus
Evidence that repeated tokens (about 4 epochs) do not hurt
Results on knowledge probes, reasoning, QA, citation prediction, chemistry, protein tasks, bias and toxicity

method.summary: Galactica trains decoder-only transformers (125M to 120B) from scratch on a curated 106B-token scientific corpus (papers, textbooks, knowledge bases, code, SMILES, protein and DNA sequences, filtered CommonCrawl) plus 358M tokens of task prompts, for 450B tokens (about 4.25 epochs). Special tokens wrap citations, step-by-step reasoning (<work>) and each sequence modality. It is evaluated zero-shot on knowledge probes, QA, MATH/MMLU, citation prediction, BIG-bench, chemistry, protein tasks and bias/toxicity.
method.task: causal language-model pretraining on a scientific corpus with prompts mixed in

datasets.name: Galactica corpus
datasets.split: validation sets held out (per-source); compound validation set 17,052; protein holdouts CASPSimSeq, PaenSeq, UniProtSeq (5,456 seqs)
datasets.source: Papers 48M docs 88B tokens (arXiv, PMC, Semantic Scholar, abstracts etc., up to July 2022); Code 2M docs 7B; Reference material 8M docs 7B; Knowledge bases 2M docs 2B; Filtered CommonCrawl 0.9M docs 1B; Prompts 1.3M docs 0.4B; Other 0.02M docs 0.2B
datasets.preprocessing: Markdown format; citations tokenised as [START_REF]title, first author[END_REF]; exact dedup of spans of 100+ bytes (Lee et al. 2022); S2 filtered by journal keywords and approximate impact factor < 1; 2M of 110M PubChem compounds and 0.5M of 227M Swiss-Prot proteins used

datasets.name: Prompt datasets (Naturebook)
datasets.source: QA, extractive QA, summarisation, entity extraction, dialog, chemical-property prompts built from public train splits (e.g. MedMCQA, PubMedQA, BioASQ, MoleculeNet train sets) plus new sets

datasets.name: Reasoning (<work>) datasets
datasets.source: GSM8k train 7,473; OneSmallStep 9,314 (50 templates); Khan Problems (AMPS) 3,835; Workout 921 hand-written

datasets.name: MMLU, MATH, ARC, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, BioASQ, MedQA-USMLE
datasets.source: Public benchmarks; in-domain where train set was in pre-training

datasets.name: PWC Citations / Extended Citations / Contextual Citations
MoleculeNet (BACE, BBBP, ClinTox, HIV, SIDER, Tox21)
datasets.size: train sets in pre-training, each example seen just over 4 times

training.objective: next-token prediction (left-to-right LM) on corpus plus prompts
training.optimizer: AdamW, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95, gradient global-norm clip 1.0
training.lr_schedule: linear decay down to 10% of its value
training.warmup: 375M tokens for 125M to 30B; 1.125B for 120B (units as printed in Table 5, no unit stated)
training.epochs: about 4.25 (450B tokens / 106B); 120B early-stopped at start of fifth epoch
training.dropout: 0.1 dropout and attention dropout; no embedding dropout
training.hardware: 128 NVIDIA A100 80GB nodes for the 120B model; inference of 120B on a single A100 node

other.note: longer warmup was important for the 120B model; authors unsure it generalises

inference.decoding: zero-shot generation unless stated; RTP: nucleus sampling
inference.samples: RTP: 25 generations per prompt for 5000 prompts; other evals single
inference.prompting: Galactica zero-shot; other LLMs 5-shot on Table 10 and BIG-bench; MATH uses <work> prompt or Minerva 5-shot mCoT
inference.retrieval: none for Galactica; sparse (ElasticSearch) and dense (Contriever, FAISS) baselines for citations

eval.protocol: Single run per size; no seeds or significance tests reported; in-domain vs out-of-domain marked per dataset

limits: No ablation separating corpus effects from prompt effects (Sec 7.1)
No comparison of prompt pre-training vs instruction tuning
Repeated-token result has no matched uncurated-corpus run; cause left open (quality vs modality)
Open-access sources only; molecule and protein data deliberately subsampled
Single run per size, no seeds or significance tests; compute not stated in GPU-hours
Context 2048 tokens; no images or 3D geometry
Some bias toward popular papers persists at 120B in citation prediction
Overfitting on out-of-domain protein set (CASPSeq) from epoch 4
Comparisons mix 0-shot Galactica with 5-shot baselines; some benchmarks are in-domain (train sets in pre-training)
Model was withdrawn from public demo shortly after release (not stated in paper)
